collection.description: A young adult is invited to race the children along the beach: race anyway, or watch and cheer.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) used to love racing the other children along the beach. Today some of the little ones are racing, and they shout for (subject.him/her) to join in. (subject) hesitates. (subject.He/She) is grown now, with work to do and things to be serious about.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) kicks off (subject.his/her) sandals and runs. (subject.He/She) loses spectacularly to (little), a six-year-old, falls into the shallows, and comes up laughing harder than (subject.he/she) has in months. Being grown up can wait until after lunch.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) sits on a rock and cheers for everybody. When (little), one of the little ones, trips, (subject) is the first to help (little.him/her) up. "You're good at cheering," (little) says. (subject) decides that's a fine thing to be good at too.
